title: Birch Star and the Lost Wisp
markdown:
The Moonmallow Mountains are very pretty. When the moon climbs up, it paints them with silver light. Little Birch Star, a young elf with hair like moonbeams, loved this time best. Birch Star walked along the sleepy cedar trail. Their feet made no sound, like little leaves. The air smelled of pine and sweet sleepy things. Birch Star’s heart felt calm and quiet.

As Birch Star walked past tall ferns, a little sound, like a tiny whisper, tickled their ears. A soft little peep. Then came a sad little whimper. Birch Star stopped and tilted their head to listen. The sound seemed to come from under a big fern. Gently, oh so gently, Birch Star lifted the fern and looked underneath with their bright eyes.

A soft little peep. That was how it began.

And there, in the soft cool moss, was a strange little creature. It was no bigger than Birch Star’s thumb, all soft fluff with tiny ears like flower petals. Its fur was pink, like the sunset, and warm. It made that little peep again, so soft it was almost lost in the rustling leaves. Its little nose wiggled, as if it were trying to find something familiar. It looked very small, and a little lost, with wide shiny eyes. This little one did not seem scary at all. It just seemed lonely.

“Oh, you poor sweet little thing. Are you lost, little one? Did you wander far from home?” The little creature blinked its big shiny eyes. It let out another soft whimper, a sound that made Birch Star’s kind heart feel a little sad. Birch Star knew right away that they must help this little creature find its way. Birch Star carefully scooped the fluffy creature into their cupped hands. They made sure their hands were warm and safe all around it, like a tiny soft nest. The creature snuggled down, making a tiny tinkling sound, like a very quiet happy little bell that only Birch Star could hear. Birch Star decided to call this little friend Wisp, because it felt so light and airy, like a whisper on the breeze.

Birch Star knew the mountains were full of kind folk. They remembered Grumbleton, the ogre who lived in a cozy cave just past the whispering willows. Grumbleton had a big warm heart. Birch Star hurried along the trail, holding Wisp gently, so the little creature felt no worry. Wisp was content, peeking out from between Birch Star’s soft hands, its petal-ears twitching a little.

They soon arrived at Grumbleton’s cave. A warm light spilled out, and the steady sound of knitting needles was comforting, like a gentle heartbeat. Grumbleton, a big ogre with kind eyes, looked up. “Well now, Birch Star. And what have we here?” His voice was deep and warm. Birch Star told him about finding Wisp, the little lost fluff. Grumbleton listened. “A lost little one. Here, take this soft scarf.” He gave Birch Star a warm scarf, yellow and blue. “Wrap your friend up warm. Sometimes a gentle song can help them remember their way home.”

Birch Star thanked Grumbleton with a happy smile and hurried on, Wisp snuggled deep inside the warm soft scarf. It smelled a little of comfort. Birch Star began to hum a little elven lullaby, a song as soft and low as a sleepy bee’s hum. As they walked, Wisp gave a little wiggle, and the tinkling sound grew louder, like tiny bells dancing. Then Birch Star heard it: soft chimes echoing from flowers ahead. Wisp perked up, its petal-ears twitching. It tumbled out of the scarf, a tiny pink fluff, and hurried towards the happy sound.

And there, gathered around the glowing flowers, were dozens of other Wisps, all making that lovely chiming sound. Their happy tinkles filled the air. They were home. The Wisp Birch Star had helped hurried towards them, its own excited tinkles joining the happy song. A Mama Wisp came closer and nudged Birch Star’s hand. It made a happy sound that felt like a warm whisper. Birch Star smiled, feeling warm all over.

As the moon climbed higher, Birch Star waved goodbye to the happy Wisp family. The sleepy cedar trail felt even more peaceful, as if it were sighing happily. Birch Star walked back towards their own cozy nook, the soft warm scarf still gently held in their hands, a sweet reminder. The trail was quiet once more, and the mountains hummed their gentle sleepy lullaby for all the creatures settling down. Birch Star snuggled into their soft moss bed, which felt like the softest cloud. The moonlight painted quiet dancing patterns on the wall. Soon Birch Star closed their bright eyes, feeling safe, warm, and very, very sleepy. A soft little peep drifted in from far away, only in a dream. Everything was just right.
characters: Birch Star (young elf with hair like moonbeams), Wisp (a pink fluff no bigger than a thumb)
